NASB.1: Hear this word which the LORD has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the entire family which He brought up from the land of Egypt:
NASB.2: 'You only have I chosen among all the families of the earth; Therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.'
NASB.3: Do two men walk together unless they have made an appointment?
NASB.4: Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl from his den unless he has captured [something]?
NASB.5: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when there is no bait in it? Does a trap spring up from the earth when it captures nothing at all?
NASB.6: If a trumpet is blown in a city will not the people tremble? If a calamity occurs in a city has not the LORD done it?
NASB.7: Surely the Lord GOD does nothing Unless He reveals His secret counsel To His servants the prophets.
NASB.8: A lion has roared! Who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken! Who can but prophesy?
NASB.9: Proclaim on the citadels in Ashdod and on the citadels in the land of Egypt and say, 'Assemble yourselves on the mountains of Samaria and see [the] great tumults within her and [the] oppressions in her midst.
NASB.10: 'But they do not know how to do what is right,' declares the LORD, 'these who hoard up violence and devastation in their citadels.'
NASB.11: Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD, 'An enemy, even one surrounding the land, Will pull down your strength from you And your citadels will be looted.'
NASB.12: Thus says the LORD, 'Just as the shepherd snatches from the lion's mouth a couple of legs or a piece of an ear, So will the sons of Israel dwelling in Samaria be snatched away-- With [the] corner of a bed and [the] cover of a couch!
NASB.13: 'Hear and testify against the house of Jacob,' Declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts.
NASB.14: 'For on the day that I punish Israel's transgressions, I will also punish the altars of Bethel; The horns of the altar will be cut off And they will fall to the ground.
NASB.15: 'I will also smite the winter house together with the summer house; The houses of ivory will also perish And the great houses will come to an end,' Declares the LORD.

AMP.1: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt:
AMP.2:
"I have known [chosen, cared for, and loved] only you of all the families of the earth;
Therefore I shall punish you for all your wickedness."
AMP.3: Do two men walk together unless they have made an appointment?
AMP.4:
Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey?
Does a young lion growl from his den if he has not captured something?
AMP.5:
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when there is no bait in it?
Does a trap spring up from the ground when it has caught nothing at all? [Of course not! So it is that Israel has earned her impending judgment.]
AMP.6:
If a trumpet is blown in a city [warning of danger] will not the people tremble?
If a disaster or misfortune occurs in a city has not the LORD caused it?
AMP.7:
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing
Without revealing His secret plan [of the judgment to come]
To His servants the prophets.
AMP.8:
The lion has roared! Who will not fear?
The Lord GOD has spoken [to the prophets]! Who can but prophesy?
AMP.9: Proclaim on the fortresses in Ashdod (Philistia) and on the citadels in the land of Egypt, and say, "Assemble yourselves on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great confusion within her and the oppressions and abuse of authority in her midst.
AMP.10: For they do not know how to do right," says the LORD, "these who store up violence and devastation [like treasures] in their strongholds."
AMP.11:
Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD,
"An adversary (Assyria), even one surrounding the land,
Shall pull down your strength from you
And your fortresses will be looted."
AMP.12:
Thus says the LORD,
"Just as the shepherd snatches from the mouth of the lion a couple of legs or a piece of the [sheep's] ear [to prove to the owner that he has not stolen the animal],
So will the [remaining] children of Israel living in Samaria be snatched away
With the corner of a bed and [part of] the damask covering of a couch.
AMP.13:
"Hear and testify against the house of Jacob,"
Says the Lord GOD, the God of hosts,
AMP.14:
"On that day when I punish Israel's transgressions,
I shall also punish the altars of Bethel [with their golden calves];
And the horns of the altar shall be cut off
And fall to the ground.
AMP.15:
"And I shall tear down the winter house with the summer house;
And the houses of ivory shall also perish
And the great houses shall come to an end,"
Says the LORD.

NLT.1: Listen to this message that the LORD has spoken against you, O people of Israel — against the entire family I rescued from Egypt:
NLT.2:
“From among all the families on the earth,
I have been intimate with you alone.
That is why I must punish you
for all your sins.”
NLT.3:
Can two people walk together
without agreeing on the direction?
NLT.4:
Does a lion ever roar in a thicket
without first finding a victim?
Does a young lion growl in its den
without first catching its prey?
NLT.5:
Does a bird ever get caught in a trap
that has no bait?
Does a trap spring shut
when there’s nothing to catch?
NLT.6:
When the ram’s horn blows a warning,
shouldn’t the people be alarmed?
Does disaster come to a city
unless the LORD has planned it?
NLT.7:
Indeed, the Sovereign LORD never does anything
until he reveals his plans to his servants the prophets.
NLT.8:
The lion has roared —
so who isn’t frightened?
The Sovereign LORD has spoken —
so who can refuse to proclaim his message?
NLT.9:
Announce this to the leaders of Philistia
and to the great ones of Egypt:
“Take your seats now on the hills around Samaria,
and witness the chaos and oppression in Israel.”
NLT.10:
“My people have forgotten how to do right,”
says the LORD.
“Their fortresses are filled with wealth
taken by theft and violence.
NLT.11:
Therefore,” says the Sovereign LORD,
“an enemy is coming!
He will surround them and shatter their defenses.
Then he will plunder all their fortresses.”
NLT.12:
This is what the LORD says: “A shepherd who tries to rescue a sheep from a lion’s mouth
will recover only two legs or a piece of an ear.
So it will be for the Israelites in Samaria lying on luxurious beds,
and for the people of Damascus reclining on couches.
NLT.13: “Now listen to this, and announce it throughout all Israel, ” says the Lord, the LORD God of Heaven’s Armies.
NLT.14:
“On the very day I punish Israel for its sins,
I will destroy the pagan altars at Bethel.
The horns of the altar will be cut off
and fall to the ground.
NLT.15:
And I will destroy the beautiful homes of the wealthy —
their winter mansions and their summer houses, too —
all their palaces filled with ivory,”
says the LORD.

MSG.1: Listen to this, Israel. God is calling you to account—and I mean all of you, everyone connected with the family that he delivered out of Egypt. Listen!
MSG.2:
"Out of all the families on earth,
I picked you.
Therefore, because of your special calling,
I'm holding you responsible for all your sins."
MSG.3:
Do two people walk hand in hand
if they aren't going to the same place?
MSG.4:
Does a lion roar in the forest
if there's no carcass to devour?
Does a young lion growl with pleasure
if he hasn't caught his supper?
MSG.5:
Does a bird fall to the ground
if it hasn't been hit with a stone?
Does a trap spring shut
if nothing trips it?
MSG.6:
When the alarm goes off in the city,
aren't people alarmed?
And when disaster strikes the city,
doesn't God stand behind it?
MSG.7:
The fact is, God, the Master, does nothing
without first telling his prophets the whole story.
MSG.8:
The lion has roared—
who isn't frightened?
God has spoken—
what prophet can keep quiet?
MSG.9:
Announce to the forts of Assyria,
announce to the forts of Egypt—
Tell them, "Gather on the Samaritan mountains, take a good, hard look:
what a snake pit of brutality and terror!
MSG.10:
They can't—or won't—do one thing right." God said so.
"They stockpile violence and blight.
MSG.11:
Therefore"—this is God's Word—"an enemy will surround the country.
He'll strip you of your power and plunder your forts."
MSG.12:
God's Message:
"In the same way that a shepherd
trying to save a lamb from a lion
Manages to recover
just a pair of legs or the scrap of an ear,
So will little be saved of the Israelites
who live in Samaria—
A couple of old chairs at most,
the broken leg of a table.
MSG.13:
"Listen and bring witness against Jacob's family"—
this is God's Word, God-of-the-Angel-Armies!
MSG.14:
"Note well! The day I make Israel pay for its sins,
pay for the sin-altars of worship at Bethel,
The horned altars will all be dehorned
and scattered around.
MSG.15:
I'll tear down the winter palace,
smash the summer palace—all your fancy buildings.
The luxury homes will be demolished,
all those pretentious houses."
God's Decree.

NIV.10:
“They do not know how to do right,” declares the Lord,
“who hoard plunder and loot in their fortresses.”
NIV.11:
Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“An enemy will overrun the land;
he will pull down your strongholds
and plunder your fortresses.”
NIV.12:
This is what the Lord says:
“As a shepherd saves from the lion’s mouth
only two leg bones or a piece of an ear,
so will the Israelites be saved,
those who sit in Samaria
on the edge of their beds
and in Damascus on their couches.”
NIV.13: “Hear this and testify against the house of Jacob,” declares the Lord, the Lord God Almighty.
NIV.14:
“On the day I punish Israel for her sins,
I will destroy the altars of Bethel;
the horns of the altar will be cut off
and fall to the ground.
NIV.15:
I will tear down the winter house
along with the summer house;
the houses adorned with ivory will be destroyed
and the mansions will be demolished,”
declares the Lord.

NET.1: Listen, you Israelites, to this message which the LORD is proclaiming against you! This message is for the entire clan I brought up from the land of Egypt:
NET.2: “I have chosen you alone from all the clans of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all your sins.”
NET.3: Do two walk together without having met?
NET.4: Does a lion roar in the woods if he has not cornered his prey? Does a young lion bellow from his den if he has not caught something?
NET.5: Does a bird swoop down into a trap on the ground if there is no bait? Does a trap spring up from the ground unless it has surely caught something?
NET.6: If an alarm sounds in a city, do people not fear? If disaster overtakes a city, is the LORD not responsible?
NET.7: Certainly the sovereign LORD does nothing without first revealing his plan to his servants the prophets.
NET.8: A lion has roared! Who is not afraid? The sovereign LORD has spoken! Who can refuse to prophesy?
NET.9: Make this announcement in the fortresses of Ashdod and in the fortresses in the land of Egypt. Say this: “Gather on the hills around Samaria! Observe the many acts of violence taking place within the city, the oppressive deeds occurring in it.”
NET.10: “They do not know how to do what is right.” (The LORD is speaking.) “They store up the spoils of destructive violence in their fortresses.
NET.11: Therefore,” says the sovereign LORD, “an enemy will encircle the land. He will take away your power; your fortresses will be looted.”
NET.12: This is what the LORD says: “Just as a shepherd salvages from the lion’s mouth a couple of leg bones or a piece of an ear, so the Israelites who live in Samaria will be salvaged. They will be left with just a corner of a bed, and a part of a couch.”
NET.13: Listen and warn the family of Jacob! The sovereign LORD, the God who commands armies, is speaking!
NET.14: “Certainly when I punish Israel for their covenant transgressions, I will destroy Bethel’s altars. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
NET.15: I will destroy both the winter and summer houses. The houses filled with ivory will be ruined, the great houses will be swept away.” The LORD is speaking!
